Independent design review — sprint `2026-09-20-review-binding-preflight`, review_run_id 208cfc50-6523-4550-b840-ac0da10815f2, mode design. Read-only; no files written. Working dir confirmed `/Users/mi_manchi/workspace/Rlues`.

1: MOSTLY CONFIRMED, two overstatements — (a) prepare hashes then writes: `_review-binding.cjs:120` precedes `:121` `append(...)`, and `append` writes `session-log.md` at `:44-51` — real. (b) `assertLive` reports field name only: `:85-89` throw the field name with no path/expected/live; for `evidence_ids` it does not even name the missing id — real. (c) stale manifest survives to ship: `accept` writes `prepared.base_commit` at `:177`, gate compares manifest to it at `delivery-gate.cjs:540-542`; nothing in prepare/bind/accept reads `implementation_commit` — real, but the manifest bytes are already bound as an evidence_doc (`:116` + `:87`), so only the commit value vs HEAD is unchecked, not manifest tampering. (d) accept regex-deletes reviewer lines: `:176` — real, but the design overstates by omission: the strip is conditional on implementation mode with an existing manifest (`:175`) and it is a deliberate, regression-tested dedup (`test_state_review.py:576-590`) that exists to satisfy the gate's exactly-one rule at `delivery-gate.cjs:525-527`. Calling it "silently rewrites the reviewer's text" without naming its purpose is not a faithful account. (e) `indexGovernanceSha256` unexported: `delivery-gate.cjs:508-512`, absent from `module.exports` at `:1434`, no caller anywhere in the tree — real on CC; on CX it is already reachable (`_review_binding.py:25-28` loads `delivery-gate.py` by path, `index_governance_sha256` at `delivery-gate.py:1141` is module-level), so "has no supported output" is a CC-only statement — CX lacks a CLI verb, not access.

2: NOT COMPLETE — `session-log.md` is not the full write set. Writers: `session-log.md` (`:44-51`), `reviews/_native/<run>-{dispatch,result}.json` (`:143-147`), `reviews/<mode>-review.md` (`:170,179`), `.ai_state/_index.md` (`:156` in bind, `:182-186` in accept). Two real holes beyond session-log: declaring `.ai_state/_index.md` as an input breaks accept's `assertLive` after bind's next_action rewrite; declaring the previous round's `reviews/<mode>-review.md` passes prepare/bind/accept (accept writes after its own assertLive) and then detonates at ship, because `validateCurrent` (`:189-192`) re-runs `assertLive` and is called from `delivery-gate.cjs:381`. Same failure class, one step later. `reviews/_native/*.json` needs no exclusion — it does not exist at prepare, so `fileRefs` (`:61-62`) already rejects it. `_index.md` is moot for the snapshot axis — `sourceSha256` skips `.ai_state` (`_input-binding.cjs:45`) — the hole reaches the manifest only through explicit `input_paths`. `excluded_inputs` is sufficient for auditability only if exclusion is applied to the stored `input_paths` as well as the hash input, because `liveInput` recomputes `fileRefs(root, prepared.input_paths)` at bind/accept/ship (`:75`).

3: AC2 IS NOT IMPLEMENTABLE FROM PERSISTED DATA — the per-entry `inputs` object built in `liveInput` (`:74-77`) is discarded; only its folded digest survives (`:79`). The prepared row persists `input_paths`, `packet_sha256`, `input_manifest_sha256`, `evidence_ids`, `evidence_docs` (`:118-120`); `evidence_docs` is the only per-path map with hashes, which is why `:87` can canonical-compare it. AC2 requires a new persisted field on a row carrying `schema_version:1` (`:118`) — a ledger schema change the design never mentions, with an unaddressed question about rows prepared before the change. Even with that field, attribution is only possible for the `fileRefs` part: `source_sha256` is a whole-tree digest (`_input-binding.cjs:40-58`) and `environment_sha256` a canonicalised env digest (`:59-76`); neither can name a file.

4: CONFIRMED CORRECT, and prepare-time is the only safe point — `accept` freezes `prepared.base_commit` (`:177`), so comparing the manifest against HEAD at prepare compares against exactly the value accept will write and the gate will demand (`delivery-gate.cjs:540`). The preflight adds no runtime `base_commit` comparison, so the deliberate tolerance at `:84` is untouched. Combined with the existing `evidence_docs` binding of the manifest bytes, prepare-time is jointly sufficient. The check is right; its implementation contract is under-specified.

5: AC4 BREAKS THE GATE'S "EXACTLY ONE" INVARIANT — `delivery-gate.cjs:522-527` (and `delivery-gate.py:1162-1168`) demand exactly one match of each `Reviewed …` line; the strip at `:176` is precisely what guarantees it, and `test_state_review.py:576-590` asserts count==1 plus removal of reviewer values. Under AC4 as written: (a) a reviewer supplying all three correct lines yields kept + prepended = 2 matches each, ship blocks with a message naming no cause; (b) partial supply is undefined; (c) a reviewer whose prose quotes a binding line at column 0 — highly likely in this project — now hard-fails the accept, and because AC4 forbids editing reviewer text the only recovery is supersede plus a whole new review round, worse than today's silent strip. Also the anchoring mismatch: the strip regex allows leading whitespace (`:176`) but the gate regex does not (`:522-524`). `validateNativeMetadata` and `explicitVerdict` are not the risk; the risk is entirely the gate's line count.

6: NO CYCLE, BUT A LOAD-PATH/EXPORT ASYMMETRY THAT KILLS AC5+AC6 — `_review-binding.cjs` already lazily requires the gate at `:36` and `:112`, and the gate lazily requires `_review-binding.cjs` at `delivery-gate.cjs:381`; the gate's only top-level effects are the `_input-binding` require (`:15`) and a `require.main` guard, so a deferred require inside a `governance` handler is precedented and safe. The real hazard: `indexGovernanceSha256` and `INDEX_GOVERNANCE_FIELDS` are not in `module.exports` (`:1434`) and CommonJS offers no other access, so AC5 forces a change to `delivery-gate.cjs`, contradicting AC6. CX has no such problem (`_review_binding.py:25-28` importlib-by-path exposes every module-level name), so the two platforms are not symmetric here.

Findings:

[P0] `design.md:49,55,63-64` (AC5 vs AC6) — AC5 and AC6 are mutually exclusive on CC and Pi. `indexGovernanceSha256` (`delivery-gate.cjs:508-512`) and `INDEX_GOVERNANCE_FIELDS` (`:502-506`) are absent from `module.exports` (`:1434`); importing them requires editing `delivery-gate.cjs`, so it cannot stay byte-identical to `0ca066c`. The same edit is needed in `vibeCoding/pi-agent/plugin/extensions/cc-core/delivery-gate.cjs:502,508`, a file the File Structure Plan does not list. Design line 55's "imports its existing export surface" is factually wrong. Resolution: relax AC6 to "delivery-gate logic unchanged; the only permitted CC/Pi diff is adding these two names to `module.exports`", with a test asserting no other line differs from `0ca066c`.

[P0] `design.md:35,60` (AC2) — AC2 promises per-path expected-vs-live attribution that the persisted ledger cannot produce. `liveInput` discards the per-entry map and stores only `input_manifest_sha256` (`_review-binding.cjs:74-79`); the prepared row (`:118-120`) has no per-input hashes, unlike `evidence_docs` which is stored per path and is therefore the one axis `assertLive` can already attribute (`:87`). Implementing AC2 requires adding a persisted per-entry map to a `schema_version:1` row and stating the behaviour for pre-existing rows — neither is in HOW or the File Structure Plan.

[P0] `design.md:45,62` (AC4) — verify-instead-of-strip can produce two matches of the same `Reviewed …` line, violating `delivery-gate.cjs:525-527` / `delivery-gate.py:1165-1168`, and it deletes the guarantee held by existing regression test `test_state_review.py:576-590` without the design acknowledging that test exists. Partial reviewer supply is undefined, and a reviewer quoting a binding line in prose becomes an unrecoverable accept failure. If AC4 is kept it must specify per-line suppress-or-prepend and prove the exactly-one invariant on all eight supply combinations.

[P1] `design.md:29,59` (AC1) — the exclusion set is stated as "the ledgers it writes" but must be "every path any of the four steps writes". Missing: `.ai_state/_index.md` (`:156`, `:182-186`) breaks accept's `assertLive` after bind; the previous round's `reviews/<mode>-review.md` (`:170,179`) survives accept and fails at ship through `validateCurrent` → `assertLive`. `reviews/_native/*.json` needs no exclusion.

[P1] `design.md:60` (AC2 wording) — "names the offending path" is unachievable for the snapshot axes. `source_sha256` and `environment_sha256` are aggregate digests with no per-file decomposition. Split AC2 into declared-input-path attribution and aggregate-axis reporting.

[P1] `design.md:41,61` (AC3) — under-specified parser and staleness definition. The gate's `parseReviewManifest` (`delivery-gate.cjs:464-499`) is a whole-file validator that also needs `pathType` (`:491`), which prepare does not have. Using it makes prepare newly hard-fail on any not-yet-ship-valid manifest (today's fixture `test_state_review.py:579` writes `schema_version: 1` alone and prepare accepts it); writing a second regex parser is the exact drift class AC5 fights. Also undefined: manifest present but `implementation_commit` absent or short-sha.

[P2] `design.md:55` — "The Pi `cc-core/_review-binding.cjs` copy is byte-identical to CC's" is false today. Two hunks differ: Pi lacks the strip line and uses `const` where CC uses `let` (`cc-core/_review-binding.cjs:165,175`). Pi is a stale pre-dedup copy that would today emit duplicate `Reviewed …` lines. State this as a defect being repaired, not as a present fact.

[P2] `design.md:29` (`excluded_inputs`) — no machine consumer. Judged justified rather than decoration, but AC1 must require a test asserting the row content, and HOW must state that exclusion applies to the stored `input_paths`, not only to the hash input.

[P2] `design.md:49,63` (AC5 mechanics) — `main`'s option whitelist (`:214`) and the `else if (!args.run) throw` chain (`:219`) mean the new verb must branch before the `--run` requirement. "Byte-identical across CC/CX" also needs a stated output format: the two field-value coercions differ in source (`delivery-gate.cjs:510` vs `delivery-gate.py:1142`), so the AC should require each side to print using its own gate's coercion and the test to diff the two outputs.

AC bijection: BROKEN — roadmap slice 3 covers issues 6, 9, 10 only, with independent acceptance point "prepare 不自毁、stale commit 提前报错、governance CLI 跨端一致". AC1+AC2 → issue 6; AC3 → issue 9; AC5 → issue 10; AC6 → standing parity invariant. AC4 maps to no roadmap issue and to no clause of slice 3's acceptance point — it is unauthorized scope, and it is simultaneously the highest-risk item. Recommend dropping AC4, or obtaining explicit user authorization plus a new roadmap issue. Conversely, AC5's dependency on a delivery-gate export change contradicts the roadmap's stated reason for serializing slices 5 and 6 on that file — the main agent should confirm a one-line export addition is acceptable before impl.

VERDICT: REWORK
